title: Potato Chips Better Than Bought
summary: Any potatoes, a vinegar soak, a stable fat. Crisp for weeks.
photoAlt: A bowl of golden homemade potato chips
intro: **Any potatoes, according to personal preference.** Soaking in vinegar water removes the starch on the outside, which causes the burning before they’re fully cooked. **DO NOT SKIP.** Forgetting to rinse will leave starch too, so **DO NOT SKIP.**

When drying on a towel, there’s no need to pat or sift or sort. Time will do the work. Once dried, at least a couple of hours, the slices will feel a bit like leather and won’t be fragile. When adding them to the fryer, add each one separately so they don’t stick together.
Use a shelf-stable fat, preferably one that’s solid on the shelf: **lard, tallow, coconut.** If you use those nasty refined cooking oils, your chips will go “stale” within a few hours.

Your chips will stay crispy and crunchy for at least a couple of weeks. With duck, goose, avocado, etc., they’ll lose their crunch in a day or two. EVOO isn’t a good choice, because it needs to be fresh oil every time: it will oxidize (go rancid) quickly.

equipment.note: A saucepan is awkward, and you need a thermometer to hold the right temperature.
Stirring the slices in the water and the fryer.

stages.title: The Cook
stages.where: Fryer at {temp:320F}, or 1 stove burner on high

steps: **Slice** to 2 mm thick. A mandoline with safety gloves is easiest.

ingredients.note: 1 cup of vinegar to 1 gallon of water

steps: **Stir** in the slices and let them sit AT LEAST 2 hours.
**Rinse** the slices until the water runs clear.
**Place** on a towel and cover with another towel, AT LEAST 2 hours. No need to pat dry.
**Fry** in batches. 4 min, flip the slices (a stir-fry strainer is handy). 4 min, flip again. 4 min, tending to the less-done slices with a spoon, until the bubbling stops.

pace.text: Have the bowl and seasoning ready: the next step comes right away.

ingredients.note: salt and pepper, sea salt, a Cajun blend, or none

steps: **Remove** to a bowl and toss with seasoning. If some aren’t done, just put them back in the fryer.

photos.caption: Chips happily sitting in water so they don’t get icky from exposure to air.
Chips in vinegar water. Notice the bit of foam starting: that’s the starch coming off.
The pot of plain water on the right is the wash-the-starch-off bath.
A stir-fry strainer moves them to a clean kitchen towel for draining. No, you don’t need to pat dry and get OCD about it.
Put the chips in the basket first. Dropping them into the oil will splatter on you, which is unpleasant.
See the chips happily frying? When the bubbles stop (the water has boiled out of the chips), they’re done.
Still in the oil, these are ready to dump in a bowl, season and toss right away.
Any seasoning will do. Or none. My favorite is salt and pepper. These 2 mm chips are strong enough for dipping. Saint Julia would be quite proud of what you did in your own kitchen. Bon appétit!

steps: **Slice** thinly. 2 mm is strong for dipping; 1.5 mm will be delicate.
**Soak** in hot water and vinegar at least 2 hours (1 cup vinegar to 1 gallon water). The water goes cloudy: that’s the starch.
**Drip-dry** on a towel, covered by a towel, at least 2 hours. They should feel slightly leathery.
**Fry** 4 min, flip. 4 min, flip. 4 min. When the bubbling stops, they’re done.
**Toss** with seasoning in a bowl. Not done? Back in the fryer.
keys: Lard, tallow or coconut: crisp for weeks
Never skip the soak or the rinse
